findings.statement: CA9 is the top convergence gene and is tumor-intrinsic: RCC cells hold a transcript share of 0.976 [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976] with immune and stromal groups near zero, and the purity-extrapolated bulk change stays large.

Against normal proximal tubule (the cell of origin), paired by donor, CA9 in tumor cells is far higher, log2FC 7.739 [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739], so the signal is tumor-cell specific and not stromal.

In Visium, CA9-high spots are enriched for RCC neighbours (log2 enrichment 0.381 [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; log2_enrichment=0.381]) and a macrophage ring is also enriched, but the composition-corrected expresser is essentially only RCC; the enrichment is modest.

AlphaFold model of CA9 has mean pLDDT 76.56 [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56]; the top cavity has volume 126.8 [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=126.8] A3 with one accessible lysine. Ligand-contact recall of detected cavities is moderate. This is a monomer heuristic and says nothing about degrons or ligase compatibility. CA9 has no dependency evidence in DepMap (ccRCC mean effect near zero), so its value is as an antibody/imaging target rather than a vulnerability.

CD70 is mainly made by RCC cells but not exclusively: RCC cells account for 0.345 of tumor transcripts by tool output, while CD8 T cells (a much larger captured population) hold the larger share, and Treg also express it; the purity-extrapolated bulk change remains clearly positive, supporting a tumor-cell component. Clinical-stage anti-CD70 antibodies already exist, so it is not novel.

KDR is an endothelial (microenvironment) target, not a tumor-cell target: endothelium holds a transcript share of 0.951 [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], consistent with anti-angiogenic TKI action.

CD74 is an antigen-presentation gene carried by immune cells (cDC, macrophage, B, pDC, monocyte), with macrophages holding a transcript share of 0.436 [gene=CD74; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.436]; a bulk CD74 signal is infiltrate, not tumor-intrinsic.

CXCR4 is expressed by lymphocytes (CD4, CD8, Treg, B); CD8 T cells alone hold a transcript share of 0.563 [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=CD8_T; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.563], so it is an immune-microenvironment target and not tumor-cell directed.

NNMT ranks high in convergence with strong tumor-up RNA that stays positive at purity 1 and adverse TCGA survival, a tumor-intrinsic metabolic enzyme; no clinical drug and DepMap shows no selective dependency, so it is a prognostic biomarker more than a proven target.

ALDOB is strongly down in tumor (negative change persists at purity 1) and low expression is associated with adverse survival in TCGA; it is a proximal-tubule loss marker, not a target for inhibition.

COL23A1 is the top tumor-track candidate: RCC cells hold a transcript share of 0.881 [gene=COL23A1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.881] (only a minority of RCC cells express it), it replicates in TCGA and stays up at purity 1 (4.88 [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]), has no adverse survival signal and no selective dependency, few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug. Surface call is 'surface' by UniProt only (SURFY and CSPA do not support it), so antibody accessibility is unconfirmed; vital-organ RNA is low. Hypothesis only.

The AlphaFold model of COL23A1 is low confidence (mean pLDDT 58.91 [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91]) and the only detected cavity is tiny and shallow, so the structure offers no small-molecule starting point; a collagen-type membrane protein would fit an antibody approach. This descriptive heuristic does not exclude other modalities.

RAB42 is a second tumor-track candidate made mostly by RCC cells, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, with very few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug; but it is an internal (non-surface) protein so not antibody-accessible, has no selective dependency and no survival signal, so it is a weak candidate until functional evidence appears.

OLFML2A is a stroma-track candidate carried by fibroblasts (source share 0.647 [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647]); it is secreted, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, with few ccRCC papers and no drug, but colon expression is the highest of the vital organs, there is no dependency evidence and fibroblast origin makes it a microenvironment, not tumor-cell, target.

JAG2 is an endothelial stroma-track Notch ligand, surface/secreted, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, no clinical drug in the screen, but with moderate literature in ccRCC and no selective dependency; it is an angiogenic-niche hypothesis whose safety in heart muscle and other tissues is unresolved.

MILR1 is the top immune-track candidate (macrophage-made, no ccRCC papers, surface, antibody-tractable) and associates with adverse TCGA survival, but its change at purity 1 shrinks to 0.414 [gene=MILR1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.414], flagged infiltration-driven; the bulk signal reflects macrophage abundance, and bone-marrow expression is a safety question.

GAL3ST4 is a macrophage-made immune-track enzyme that is replicated in TCGA, purity-robust and linked to adverse survival, with very few ccRCC papers; it is an internal enzyme (not antibody-accessible) with no dependency data, so only a prognostic or myeloid-state marker hypothesis at present.

LILRB4 is a macrophage surface checkpoint-like receptor; its tumor-up signal is infiltration-driven (vanishes in a pure tumor) and replicates in TCGA, with moderate ccRCC literature; a microenvironment immunotherapy hypothesis, not a tumor-cell target.

caveats: EPAS1, MET and EGFR were not queried in this run; only CA9, KDR, CD74, CXCR4, CD70 and the top-ranked genes were covered.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses; none has selective DepMap dependency or functional evidence, and literature is counted by gene symbol.
Single-cell captures are unbalanced (many T cells), so transcript shares depend on cell counts; cpm_share was not used for most claims. Some RCC cell groups come from few donors.
Structural scores are monomer heuristics and do not identify degrons, ligase compatibility or predict degradation.
For CD70 the quoted shares come from a record without an evidence id for the RCC group; only purity/TCGA/omics ids are cited.
ALDOB and NNMT statements rely on convergence_ranking outputs; details are in the cited purity and survival records.
